component: Installed distribution identity versus static source metadata
constraints: Compare name and version in the current interpreter distribution metadata with static pyproject.toml values, without a second version constant or executing source build scripts.
Existing Python 3.9/3.13 developer CI matrix; no runtime dependency change, network lookup during checking, throughput or hard-real-time requirement.
alternatives: Python tomllib plus pinned Tomli on Python below 3.11, with importlib.metadata.
Rust uv inspection with TOML/package metadata orchestration.
Java TomlJ parsing with a Python interpreter metadata probe.
Go TOML parsing and interpreter subprocess inspection; discovery page was unavailable, so no unsupported capability claim informs selection.
rationale: KEEP same-interpreter metadata inspection and use standard TOML parsing. The required values already reside in pyproject.toml; parsing them directly avoids inventing a subset parser or maintaining a duplicate version flag.

Python 3.11 introduced tomllib. Tomli documents the conditional compatibility pattern and its 2.5.0 package supports Python >=3.8. The existing declared metadata uses TOML syntax understood by both; this does not claim equivalence for all TOML features.

TomlJ provides Java TOML parsing and uv provides package tooling. These are credible options, but a separate process still must identify the tested Python environment and implement the static equality gate. No requirement justifies an added orchestration boundary here.

Four methods use real temporary METADATA and pyproject files. They reject wrong/missing installed fields, invalid static source version declarations and duplicate TOML keys. A no-op sensitivity control produces ten expected assertion failures across three negative methods.
limits: This compares exact declared strings for this project profile, not all equivalent normalized package names or PEP 440 version spellings. Dynamic name/version is rejected, not resolved.
Local tests and isolated installed check use Linux Python 3.13 only. Python 3.9/Tomli and the hosted matrix remain unobserved; no alternate-language performance benchmark.
Metadata is a trusted local build input. This is not publisher authentication, full metadata schema validation, package __version__ validation, dependency closure or source provenance attestation.
No new installation/build/clean clone, operational runtime or hardware behavior.
